messages:
Maya: Heads-up — kv cache long-context bench on master is regressing. Memory keeps growing throughout the synthetic longflow sweep and we see eviction spikes followed by excessive paging. Uploaded the raw run: https://perf.internal/runs/1867923456 :eyes:

perf-bot: benchmark run 1867923456 uploaded to perf dashboard (kvcache-longflow / synthetic-sweep).

Maya: Quick summary blob from the run:
```
KVCache longflow synthetic sweep - summary
- config: tokens=1_000_000, seq_lens=[8,64,1024,2048], interleaved reuse
- kv_page_size=64MB, compaction_interval=300s, prefix_cache=on
- start_mem=2.1GB, mem@200k=3.4GB, mem@1M=7.6GB
- growth_rate ~ 5.5MB / 10k tokens
- fragmentation_estimate=42% (from heap-slab-metrics)
- evictions_total=12_132, page_faults=8_024
```

Liam: Can you attach the heap profile / flamegraph? also which allocator build? jemalloc or tcmalloc?

Maya: Attached: /artifacts/1867923456/heap.prof and /artifacts/1867923456/flame.svg
Allocator: jemalloc (build tag enable_xmalloc=false).

Sophia: Noting that the kernel-selection patch from last week switched to fused-attn kernels for 2k+ contexts. Could be influencing slot lifetime and preventing reuse of small fragments. Did you try forcing legacy kernels?

Maya: Tried ENABLE_LEGACY_KERNELS=1 for a short run — growth rate dropped ~18% but still nontrivial. Re-ran with compaction_interval=30s and that reduced peak growth by ~40%, but memory still drifts upward over long runs.

Daniel: Can you paste the bench command you used so I can repro locally?

Maya: Command used:
```
./bench_longflow \ 
  --model redwood-v2-small \ 
  --tokens 1000000 \ 
  --seq-mix 8:0.5,64:0.2,1024:0.2,2048:0.1 \ 
  --kv-page-size 64MB \ 
  --compaction-interval 300 \ 
  --reuse-pattern interleaved \ 
  --seed 42
```

Sophia: Two lines to triage from my end:
- Investigate fragmentation: add a forced compaction sweep at 60s and instrument slot reuse hits/misses per page.
- Check kernel path where fused-kernel allocates temporary KV buffers; ensure they go through the same slab pools as persistent slots.

Maya: Added extra telemetry in the next run: slot_reuse_hits, slot_reuse_misses, page_compactions, slab_free_chunks. Run id 1867923601 (perf-bot uploaded). Early numbers: reuse_hits/reuse_misses = 3.2k / 9.1k (bad), compactions=14, slab_free_chunks increased then plateaued.

perf-bot: run 1867923601 results: https://perf.internal/runs/1867923601 (attached CSV).

Liam: If reuse misses are that high, could be an alignment / header size change after kernel patch. Also check if sequence-length distribution produces a lot of ephemeral slots that block reuse (very short magic sequences interleaved with long).

Maya: I also tried toggling prefix_cache off. That reduced eviction churn but increased token compute cost; mem growth still present but slightly lower.

Daniel: Proposed quick mitigations to test in CI-regression harness:
- lower default compaction_interval to 60s for longflow suite
- enable opportunistic merging of adjacent free fragments during compaction
- add targeted stress test with repeated interleaved small/huge sequences to maximize fragmentation

Sophia: Agree. Also add a guard in kernel selection to keep legacy kernels for seq_len >= 1024 until we confirm fused path preserves slot lifetimes.

Maya: I'll spin a PR with tests + altered compaction default for the kvcache-longflow regression job. Draft here: https://git.internal/r/adk/kvcache/merge/PR-5234 — includes new telemetry counters and a harness variant run_small_frag_repeat.

Liam: I'll take the initial investigation. Assigned to @Liam.

Maya: Thanks. Quick notes for postmortem: this looks like fragmentation + missed reuse rather than a pure allocator leak; compaction helps but doesn't fully close the gap. Next steps: reproduce with isolated alloc trace, compare fused vs legacy kernel runs, add unit test that asserts reuse_miss_rate < 0.5 for 1M-token sweep. :+1:

ops-bot: Reminder — please tag the incident if this impacts customer SLAs. Currently no customer reports.

Sophia: I'll follow up with a microbenchmark that allocates KV slots from both kernel paths and checks slab ownership / trailing bytes.

Maya: Cool. I'll leave artifacts and a short repro shell in the PR. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
